topics.include: Prompt explicitly asks for a name, caption, fictional dialogue/story, visual design, verbal image, written performance or discussion of books/art.
topics.exclude: Ordinary answering or reading UI alone does not qualify. A creative task can also require food, music or other subject tags; this is never a replacement for those tags.

topics.include: Explicit magic, personified inanimate objects, impossible transformations, invented creatures/worlds or deliberately absurd physical scenarios.
topics.exclude: Merely hypothetical everyday choices, fictional examples of normal life, a drawn object or a musical metaphor need not imply an impossible fictional world.

topics.include: A concrete manufactured object, furnishing, clothing item, package/container, stationery, craft or appliance is itself a character, has its identity/role/physical features described, supplies the imagined setting/container, or is a substantive metaphor/comparison. Negated objects still count when their absence is part of the requested scene.
topics.exclude: Writing an answer or making a caption/postcard does not alone make its output medium an object subject. Mere room occurrence uses places_travel. A named prop that is only incidental background need not count. Instruments use music_sound, with everyday_objects added when material/structure is itself discussed. Food on containers is contextual, not automatic.

labels.ru: Еда, напитки и посуда для них

topics.include: Food/drink, ingredients, flavours, cooking, cafés/menus, meals/picnics, cups/kettles/saucepans or food metaphors appear in any card side, even an optional example.
topics.exclude: Personal aesthetic taste is not food. Non-food jars, lids and boxes do not necessarily imply eating; the context determines whether food utensils are involved.

topics.include: Named or invented places, room layouts, imagined cities/venues, routes, maps, transport, travel or spatial journey metaphors are substantive content.
topics.exclude: Private channel, room ID and meeting_context metadata are not geographical topics. A bare metaphorical inner part does not automatically describe a physical place.

topics.include: Plants/animals, weather/seasons, celestial objects, landscapes, natural water/ice or explicit nature comparisons are substantive prompt content, including named examples. An unspecified transparent water drop used as a shape/image is conservatively natural water; a leaf or rain example independently establishes nature.
topics.exclude: Generic colour, human mood, everyday sound drip and an explicitly household tap drop with no natural comparison are not nature. Fictional dragons are fiction; realistic animal types such as cats, owls and hedgehogs also receive nature. Food liquids and an imagined sea of lemonade are food/fiction/place content, not automatically natural water.

topics.include: Music, instruments, genres, melodies, timbre, rhythm, audio backgrounds, sound descriptions, acoustics or deliberate sonic silence are subjects.
topics.exclude: Life pace, written-note wording, personal voice/style and a quiet social atmosphere are not automatically musical. Tag sound only when the prompt actually discusses hearing, sound or deliberate acoustic absence.

topics.include: Hobbies, reading as an activity, board games/riddles as shared leisure, holidays/days off, festivals/celebrations, recreational walks, magic shows or cinema.
topics.exclude: The fact that Venus is a game does not classify every prompt as leisure. Creative production is also tagged creative_expression where explicit; a standalone wording puzzle is humour/creative expression without necessarily a leisure scene.

topics.include: Explicit joke, pun, amusing/funny result, word puzzle/riddle, comic exaggeration, humorous instruction/title or absurd bureaucratic claim.
topics.exclude: Not every fictional world or warm exchange is humour. Consent/refusal examples are not comic merely because a character speaks.

labels.tr: Arkadaşlık, birlikte olma ve iş birliği

topics.include: Friends, friendly care, shared social rituals, companionship, a narrative team/shared project, recognition, gifts or cooperation are substantive subjects.
topics.exclude: P1/P2 placeholders, bilateral workflow and two people composing an unrelated answer do not by themselves mean friendship. This tag does not imply romance or a relationship outside the room.

topics.include: An explicit interpersonal intent or speech act is the requested subject/outcome: invitation or coordinating signal, greeting/introduction (including CV self-presentation), thanks/cheer, apology, refusal, request/application, complaint, account of a character's own conduct, announcement, clarification, listening, advice/support, turn-taking or conversational closing/change. Fictional speakers count. Explicit communication wording/style or who receives a disclosure also counts.
topics.exclude: Generic answer/write/discuss/exchange procedure, arbitrary questions about another subject, arbitrary dialogue/argument, personal inner-character dialogue, artistic letters as a medium, news/forecast/report/expository explanation and advertising text without the listed interpersonal purpose do not by themselves qualify. Every YesBut offer/responder consent/stop instruction is procedure, not its subject.

topics.include: Explicit pressure-free choice, declining/advice permission, opting to observe, changed decisions, private meaning/disclosure, preserving unknown details, personal enoughness or sensory load/autonomy are central subjects, including metaphors.
topics.exclude: Mandatory if-you-wish/stop/consent boilerplate does not add this tag by itself. An ordinary choice of colour or object is not automatically a boundary exercise.

topics.include: An explicitly personal mood, comfort, aesthetic preference, routine, remembered pleasure, attention, sense of ownership or creative self-portrait is requested; invented answers may remain possible.
topics.exclude: P1/P2 naming and choosing a detail in a purely fictional neutral task do not alone make the subject personal. This is not counselling, trauma, diagnosis or an assertion about a participant.

policy.scope: Subjects explicitly present in service card text, including optional examples and all localized sides; not participant free speech or future user-authored conditions.
policy.union_rule: Union across question or both truth/dare or proposal/responder, and RU/EN/TR; any excluded tag blocks the whole service prompt under a future separately reviewed policy.
policy.boilerplate_rule: Invitation/action consent and stop boilerplate are procedure, not automatically personal_boundaries or communication_support topics.
policy.category_rule: Historical category is metadata only and is never used as an exhaustive subject classifier.
policy.unknown_rule: Unknown ID/revision/hash, missing locale, unknown topic or unresolved required review is not eligible for promotion.
policy.romance: No new romance taxonomy inferred from private transport or pair metadata. The13inherited subjects are candidate annotations only; human editorial/language review remains required for470.
policy.response_scope: No promise that human free-text answers, advice or YesBut conditions stay inside these subjects. New condition/topic content needs its own policy and new bilateral consent.
